entities.summary: The Metamorphosis is a novella by Franz Kafka, written in 1912. It tells the story of Gregor Samsa, a traveling salesman who transforms into a giant insect. The novella explores themes of isolation, identity, and the absurdity of modern life. Kafka's unique narrative style and exploration of the human condition have made The Metamorphosis a classic of modernist literature. The novella has been translated into numerous languages and has had a significant impact on 20th-century literature, influencing authors such as Albert Camus and Jean-Paul Sartre. Its exploration of the human condition and the absurdity of modern life continues to resonate with readers today. The Metamorphosis is a testament to Kafka's genius as a writer and his ability to capture the complexities of the human experience.
